assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the subject's one curated REVIEWED item at basis_commit, read end to end with its front matter: the canonical V2 individual character monograph series/lycoris-recoil/03 V2 Working Artifacts/05 Specialist Synthesis/LYCORIS_RECOIL_ITO_CHARACTER_SYNTHESIS.md (22,109 bytes, status canonical, empty supersession arrays, do_not_use_as_current_authority false), a portrait of Itō (伊藤) in Asaura's Japanese prose: the Recovery days manuscript commission 'Safety work' (S10) and its reference back in 'Cough' (S12); in Ordinary days the group reference shoot (S15), the cover and the Kana sequence (S17-S18) and the magazine context (S19, S22); in Gluttony days only a saying Chisato quotes (S14); located by spine item and paragraph. The discovery row claims behavior, psychology, relationships and decision-making, and does not claim speech or ethics. She has no television identity. The sequential readings, crosswalk and readiness record the portrait links are not curated on this subject; no claim rests on them, and the readiness record was read only as calibration input. The project's COMPLETE_AT_BOUNDARY outcome was not adopted as a grade. No primary source was inspected for this assessment.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: The A2 novels as the portrait locates them, with no order asserted between the books: the portrait says the Ordinary days serial is not confirmed as the outcome of the Recovery days one-shot (15.30-39, 18.74-80; 10.279-294). Recovery days states in order: the counter request after she has already used the partners as models (10.2-89); the apartment session, the poses and the hand correction (10.159-280); the prop critique and the deadline-versus-reference choice (10.298-369); the replacement reference, posed and photographed (10.369-423); the meal (10.421-558); the discharge (10.559-592); waking to the partners' account and finishing the pages (10.570-702); the cooling sheets during Chisato's illness (12.105-116, 12.393-404). Ordinary days states: the group reference shoot (15.14-58); the cover and the question to Kana (17.10-91); after closing, the finished line art and the money question (18.2-99). Gluttony days: a remembered saying (14.199-215). Her background (having lived near Kana's school, her working practice) belongs to her at every located state. The split falls at the discharge: before it she believes the reference is a replica; after it she holds the partners' account of a dropped replica, and no scene shows her learning otherwise.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, applying the owner calibration rulings recorded there (B/C boundary, single counting of uncertainty, dialogue constrained-use test, chronology splits, relationship-transfer safeguards and control-state attribution) and the owner's A/B boundary direction of 24 November 2026 in PR #694, not yet recorded in the policy: A turns on the integration, individuation and transferability of the model within a declared scope; interpretations that predict the same behavior may coexist; divergent transfer conditions, missing evidence and unsettled dispositions are named and excluded rather than counted against the tier; held-out validation, analytical derivation, relationship labels and preserved source chronology are not barriers. Evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: Within professional reference work the portrait explains what changes her decision: she revises when another person can show her what a reader will see differently, reversing her judgment of Chisato's hand and adding a close-up (10.239-280); she takes a prop error seriously because readers will pillory it online and rejects a defense of artistic license (10.298-345); she keeps her chosen angle and declines the CG route or an online photograph because of her technical limits and the risk of a tracing accusation (10.159-175, 10.318-345); she weighs the best reference against a scarce editorial opening, says why 'other chances' do little for her, and returns to the tablet (10.348-369); she hands coloring to a designer when time and stamina run short (18.2-18). It predicts her mistakes: using the partners as models before asking (10.55-89), pressing Kana for an anecdote while absorbed in drawing and missing her distress (17.36-91), an assumption about a girl's spending (18.33-63), and trusting a friend's account of a reference that is a real firearm (10.369-395, 10.559-592). Not A: one commission carries most of the evidence, and the portrait leaves open her response to revoked permission, to a disclosure about the accident and to an editor's decision. Not C: the account discriminates the conditions of revision and refusal and says where it stops; whether she made peace with the deadline is uncertain affect, not an undecided motive.

Ordered states with triggers within Recovery days, from the request after use to the finished pages and the cooling sheets (10.2-702, 12.105-116, 12.393-404), and within Ordinary days, from the shoot to the cover, the Kana question and the finished line art (15.14-58, 17.10-91, 18.2-99). Not B: no development is claimed across states, and the order between the books is not established (15.30-39; 10.279-294). Not D: the states within each book are located with their triggers.

The row does not claim speech. The portrait briefly describes register: informal, appreciative Japanese with willing helpers (15.30-58); a switch to polite speech for the precise request to pose, explained only as 'just because' (10.165-186); 「私」 for the artist stating her technical limits and in the shocked, broken sentences about her tablet and pages (10.159-175, 10.559-576); the joke about kneeling for permission after the fact (10.55-89). Not C: few forms are quoted, and the portrait places the variation in written speech and narrative timing without a performed voice. Not E: a register shift tied to the kind of request is analyzed.

Located working habits: a café table wide enough for a notebook, pens or a tablet (10.2-55); an apartment studio full of books, inking on paper and finishing digitally (10.159-175); working through the night, with the editor's morning arrival as the real deadline (10.659-675, 14.199-215); telling guests to keep their voices down and letting them use the refrigerator (10.168-180, 10.421-463); sending cooling sheets from what she had on hand (12.393-404). Not B: her life outside work is thin, and the visitors cannot tell whether her sparse refrigerator reflects her hours or her taste (10.529-558). Not D: several distinct routines are located.

Directed differences: Chisato as her easiest companion, who makes a game of a desperate pitch, comments honestly while always finding something to praise, and draws her into talk and matchmaking jokes (10.34-89, 18.2-18, 15.65-85); Takina, asked formally, and the source of a correction she dreads (10.165-186, 10.298-345); Yoneoka, judged with 'I mustn't end up like that' (18.2-18); Kana, addressed while she keeps drawing, and missed (17.36-91); the regulars at the shoot, invited to request changes (15.30-51); the editor as a timetable (10.659-675). Not B: most differences come from two partners within one commission, the others are single scenes, and the café's operational life is withheld from her. Not D: the differences are located with what produces them.

Her own thoughts are rendered after closing in Ordinary days: appreciation of Chisato, judgment of Yoneoka and pride in finishing her share (18.2-18), and her reasoning about Kana's journeys (18.33-63). Not B: Safety work is largely seen through Takina, and the reading that she put the deadline first without making peace with it is Takina's (10.348-369). Not D: a located passage of her own reasoning.

Located: telling the partners to keep their voices down in her home (10.421-463); rejecting Chisato's defense of artistic license once the word mistake is used (10.298-345); keeping her angle against the CG suggestion (10.159-175); challenging two alternatives about Kana until Mika stops the prying (18.33-63); her bewildered first words after the discharge (10.559-592). Not C: the disagreements are brief and mostly about the work; no conflict with a person is sustained, and an objection from a model or an editor's refusal is untested. Not E: several located disagreements with their conditions.

The row does not claim ethics. Located: she uses the partners' likeness before asking and jokes about kneeling for permission after the fact (10.55-89); she invites her photographed subjects to request changes (15.30-51); she distinguishes tracing her own reference from being accused of tracing an online photograph (10.318-345); Mika, not she, ends the prying about Kana (18.33-63). Not C: no weighing of her own is rendered on these questions. Not E: the portrait analyzes the separate permission questions her conduct raises.

Located: the kneeling joke (10.55-89); improvising future serial developments with Chisato while Takina holds the pose (10.215-243); laughing at Takina's report of Chisato reading in bed and calling them a good pair (10.491-519); the far-fetched wish to marry Chisato to a son she does not have (15.65-85). Not C: the play is brief and mostly with Chisato. Not E: several located instances.

The portrait covers her appearances across Recovery days, Ordinary days and the Gluttony days saying with spine-and-paragraph locators and keeps others' readings attributed: Takina's reading of the deadline choice, Tokuda's view of the Kana question, the partners' account of the discharge, Chisato's quotation of her saying. Not A: one derived item, and speech and ethics are not claimed. Not C: her located appearances are covered and attributed.

Located bounds against overreading: no scene shows her learning the firearm's origin, approving Kurumi's delay of the editor or learning the terms of her rescue, and the cooling sheets do not suggest she learned the truth (10.570-702, 12.393-404); payment is put off with no amount and no agreement that the work was free (10.675-702); the sparse refrigerator cannot be read as her taste (10.529-558); the matchmaking establishes no son and no romantic history (15.65-85); she neither took nor released the magazine's candid pancake picture (22.2-56); the Ordinary days serial is not confirmed as the outcome of the one-shot (15.30-39, 10.279-294); her silence under the cheering is weaker evidence than her stated resolve (10.698-702). Not A: no forecast is tested against later evidence. Not C: each bound is located.

Within Safety work the order is located by paragraph, from the counter request to the finished pages, with the editor's morning arrival as the deadline (10.659-675); her age is given as around thirty. Not C: the order between the books is not established and no intervals between her café visits are given. Not E: the order within each story is located.

scenario_readiness.note: The row does not claim speech; the portrait describes her register only briefly, quotes few forms and gives no performed voice.

conditions: A café regular or helper shows her, during reference work she has permission for, a detail a reader would see differently: predict that she notes it, changes the panel on the spot if the idea excites her, and weighs what it adds against the deadline (10.239-280, 15.30-51; the portrait's closing paragraph).
A correction that exposes a mistake readers would notice: predict that she takes it seriously and does not accept artistic license as a defense (10.298-345).
An apparently easier route that changes the angle she has chosen or relies on someone else's online image: predict that she keeps the angle and declines (10.159-175, 10.318-345).

A scarce opening on deadline against a better reference: predict that she returns to work toward delivery and delegates part of the job when time and stamina run short; that she has not made peace with the choice is Takina's reading (10.348-369, 18.2-18).
A reference or help supplied by a trusted friend: predict that she accepts the friend's account without checking it (10.369-395, 10.559-592).

Include her mistakes: using a likeness before asking (10.55-89); pressing a young customer for an anecdote while absorbed in drawing and missing the distress (17.36-91); assumptions about other people's spending (18.33-63).

Exclude: a model revoking approval after the page is finished; learning the truth about the tablet or the firearm; an editor's serialization decision; the café's operational life; romance; and anything that needs a performed voice.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: Recovery days 'Safety work' through 'Cough' and the Ordinary days shoot, cover and Kana scenes, with no order asserted between the books; split at the discharge, after which she holds the partners' account of a dropped replica.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Chisato and Takina as models and helpers; café regulars (Tokuda, Doi, Yoneoka, Kana) and Mika as café company; the editor offstage. A comparable new model or helper is a separate, lower-confidence condition.
setting_constraints: Her apartment studio and Café LycoReco during work on a manuscript or illustration.
No television identity, and no outcome invented to settle a prediction.

scenario_readiness.note: Narrow extrapolation from the portrait's closing paragraph and the located acts it rests on, within professional reference work. Revoked permission, disclosure of the accident and an editor's decision are excluded.

conditions: Working at a café table among regulars, sharing a meal cooked by her helpers, telling guests to be quiet in her home, and returning care with what she has on hand (10.2-55, 10.421-558, 12.393-404, 18.2-18).
Excluded: home routines outside work, her family, and any social circle beyond the café.
scenario_readiness.note: Her café and studio company is located; her life outside work is not.
The row does not claim ethics; the permission questions her conduct raises are analyzed by the portrait, but no deliberation of hers is rendered (10.55-89, 15.30-51).
The matchmaking jokes establish no son and no romantic history for her, and no romance is analyzed (15.65-85).

conditions: Reference and revision work on a manuscript or illustration under deadline: posing and photographing helpers, accepting reader-visible corrections, keeping a chosen angle, delegating coloring, and timing delivery to the editor's morning arrival (10.159-369, 10.659-702, 15.30-51, 18.2-18).
Excluded: negotiation with an editor, the outcome of a serialization bid, payment terms with her helpers, and a mystery commission she has never drawn (10.675-702, 18.70-99).
scenario_readiness.note: Her manga practice is the best-located part of the evidence; its commercial outcomes are not.

known_limits.statement: She has no scene of learning the firearm's origin, approving Kurumi's delay of the editor or learning the full terms of her rescue; the account she is given attributes the damage to a dropped replica (10.570-702, 12.393-404).
That she put the deadline first without making peace with it is Takina's reading of a working artist facing two losses, not her stated view (10.348-369).
The Ordinary days serial with a Chisato-modeled lead is not confirmed as the outcome of the Recovery days one-shot, and the quarterly commission has no settled genre (15.30-39, 18.74-80, 10.279-294).
Payment for the helpers' work is put off, with neither an amount nor an agreement that it was free (10.675-702).
Her matchmaking and the wish about a son she does not have establish neither a son nor a romantic history (15.65-85).
Whether her sparse refrigerator reflects her working hours or her taste cannot be told (10.529-558).
No scene tests her response to a model revoking approval after the page is finished, a disclosure about the accident, or an editor's actual decision about a serial.
Speech is not claimed on the row and the portrait gives no performed voice, so no register can be modeled beyond the few located forms.
